title: Riverton and Seaview
body: Riverton is an old trading city built about 80 km inland on the bank of a wide river that flows into the sea. Flat-bottomed ships and barges sail up the river to Riverton's docks. The port mainly handles packaged products and manufactured goods, and a terminal there also carries thousands of passengers every week. As world trade grew, cargo ships became too large to sail up the river to Riverton. The port authority therefore built a new deep-water port called Seaview on the coast at the river mouth. Very large ships now unload at Seaview, and their cargo is then carried to Riverton and its hinterland. Each year the authority publishes the tonnage of cargo and the number of ships handled at both ports.
